issues.fix: Enlarge the tiles to 44 px and darken the glyph strokes to at least 4.5:1 against the tile fill

issues.problem: The interaction marker (heart and hand) is small and sits in busy grass, so it takes a second look to find.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 2: state clear within 1 s
issues.fix: Give the marker a soft 4 px cream halo and scale it about 1.3×

issues.region: top-right gear, white blossom highlights top-right tree
issues.problem: Near-pure white appears on the gear icon and the blown blossom highlights, which breaks the otherwise warm-tinted palette.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 3: no pure black or white
issues.fix: Clamp the highlights and UI white to a warm cream (about #F6EFDD)

issues.problem: The saturated orange flower cluster is one hot accent that pulls away from the controlled greens and violets.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 3: controlled saturation
issues.fix: Lower the saturation of the orange flowers by about 15%

issues.problem: The rock facets have sharp creases and jagged silhouette edges, unlike the rounded toy forms elsewhere in the scene.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 5: every edge beveled or rounded
issues.fix: Apply a chamfer/bevel modifier to the rock meshes and soften the normals

issues.problem: The bright, sharp foreground lupins and bushes compete with the central ruin for attention.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 6: one obvious focal point
issues.fix: Add a slight depth-of-field blur and drop foreground exposure by about 10% so the eye settles on the ruin

issues.problem: The toolbar sits on top of busy foreground flowers, and the bottom-left bush is cut awkwardly by the frame edge.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 7: no awkward tangents
issues.fix: Tilt the camera about 3° upward, or add a soft 60 px bottom vignette behind the toolbar

issues.problem: The canopies crowd the top edge and leave little breathing room above the ruin.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 7: breathing room
issues.fix: Pull the camera back about 5% or trim the canopy radius of the nearest trees

issues.problem: The tile fills vary (orange, olive, teal, cream) with no visible selected or hover state, and the glyph stroke weights differ slightly between icons.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 9: one icon stroke weight, visible states
issues.fix: Normalise all glyphs to one 2 px stroke and add a 2 px raised outline plus lift to mark the active tile

issues.problem: The grass-card clumps repeat noticeably across the lower-right lawn.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 10: no visible tiling
issues.fix: Randomise the rotation, scale (±20%) and hue jitter of the grass instances

issues.problem: The pale glyphs on light tiles (terrain, image, sun) have low contrast.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 11: contrast ≥ 4.5:1 in principle
issues.fix: Darken these glyphs to a deep brown (about #3A2A1E)

issues.problem: The red and green flower accents carry no secondary cue, although nothing gameplay-critical depends on them.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 11: colour + glyph identity
issues.fix: Keep any interactive marker using shape plus colour (heart silhouette), and never rely on red vs green alone

issues.problem: The stock-looking white gear is the one element that reads as template UI.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 15: premium indie gut check
issues.fix: Replace it with an illustrated gear on a parchment tile that matches the toolbar

issues.problem: The alpha-cut leaf edges show slight dithered or aliased fringing against the bright sky gaps.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 18: no aliasing
issues.fix: Enable alpha-to-coverage on the foliage material with MSAA 4×

issues.problem: Faint shadow banding appears across the grass behind the right ruin.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 18: no banding
issues.fix: Add blue-noise dithering to the shadow and fog output

issues.problem: Voter name tags (PHIL, ALEX, LUKE) are about 12 px caps at 720p and get soft at stream quality; the prompt's thin dark outline also blurs a little on the green
issues.rule: RUBRIC item 2 '10 looks like': critical text ≥ 22 px at 1080p
issues.fix: Raise tag labels to ≥ 16 px at 720p and thicken the prompt's outline from about 1 px to 2 px

issues.problem: The grey tombstone avatar and the grey BROOKE credit are close to neutral grey, which clashes with the tinted palette everywhere else
issues.rule: RUBRIC item 3: tinted shadows, no off-palette greys
issues.fix: Tint the grey toward the lavender of the bubble (for example #8C8A9E instead of neutral grey)

issues.problem: The bubbles are lit fairly flat and have only a faint contact shadow, so they lift less off the tunnel than the clay avatars do
issues.rule: RUBRIC item 4: pieces lift off the board
issues.fix: Add a soft, green-tinted drop shadow (about 12 px blur at 25% opacity) below each bubble

issues.problem: The prompt is less prominent than the two answers, so the eye lands on the bubbles before it knows what they answer
issues.rule: RUBRIC item 6: eye moves action → state → context
issues.fix: Scale the prompt up about 15% or give it a subtle backing plate

issues.problem: The lower band of the frame, between the two avatars, is empty tunnel, so the composition sits top-heavy
issues.rule: RUBRIC item 7: breathing room without dead space
issues.fix: Move the bubble pair down about 30 px or reserve the band for a vote tally

issues.problem: The prompt's two-line break leaves a short second line ('dating profile') that reads as a near-widow
issues.rule: RUBRIC item 8: no widows
issues.fix: Rebalance the break to 'The most intriguing phrase / to find in a dating profile'

issues.problem: The four voter tags overlap and stagger unevenly (LIZ sits behind LUKE and ANDY), and the spacing differs from the neat two-tag row on the left
issues.rule: RUBRIC item 9: consistent 4-pt spacing, no clipping
issues.fix: Stack the tags in a regular 2×2 grid with 4 px gaps

issues.problem: The clay tunnel texture is slightly soft or blurred at the edges compared with the crisp bubble texture
issues.rule: RUBRIC item 10: no blurry art
issues.fix: Use a higher-resolution tunnel texture or limit the depth-of-field blur to the far center

issues.problem: PHIL, ALEX and LUKE all use similar olive or green tags, so these players are told apart by label text alone and not by colour
issues.rule: RUBRIC item 11: colour + glyph identity
issues.fix: Give each player a distinct hue plus their avatar glyph on the tag

issues.problem: The vote reveal does not show a tally or winner call-out, so the result is inferred by counting tags
issues.rule: RUBRIC item 13: result stated clearly
issues.fix: Add a vote count badge (for example '2' vs '4') to each bubble

issues.problem: The flat lighting on the bubbles slightly undercuts the premium clay feel
issues.rule: RUBRIC item 15: premium indie gut check
issues.fix: Apply the bubble shadow and lighting fix from CAL-R1-03

issues.problem: The 'jackbox.tv' URL above the room code is small (about 11 px) and low contrast on the dark plate
issues.rule: RUBRIC item 17: room code legible
issues.fix: Raise the URL to ≥ 14 px and lighten it to about 90% white

issues.problem: There is slight edge aliasing on the lavender bubble silhouettes against the dark green
issues.rule: RUBRIC item 18: no aliasing
issues.fix: Enable 4× MSAA or add a 1 px feathered edge to the bubble sprites

issues.problem: The glossy yellow slab-serif prompt with its hard drop shadow reads more like a broadcast lower-third than the matte clay of the cards and characters.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 1 (one cohesive world); §4.1 reference band, minor flaw -0.1
issues.fix: Set the prompt on a small clay/paper plaque, or give it a softer tinted shadow (2 px offset, 40% deep-teal) in place of the hard black one

issues.problem: The author names are small (about 18 px at 720p) and grey or purple on lavender, so at stream quality they take a second look to read.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 2 (critical text ≥ 22 px at 1080p, clear within 1 s); minor -0.2
issues.fix: Raise the author labels to at least 24 px at 720p and darken them to the card's ink colour

issues.region: player tags top of both cards
issues.problem: The cyan ANDY and orange LIZ tags are noticeably more saturated than the muted teal and lavender field, and they pull hot.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 3 (controlled saturation); minor -0.2
issues.fix: Drop tag saturation about 15% and shift the cyan toward the teal family

issues.problem: The cards are lit evenly and flat, so they don't pick up the tunnel's central green glow and float a little apart from the scene.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 4 (pieces lift through light); minor -0.2
issues.fix: Add a faint green rim on the inner edges of the cards and a soft tinted contact shadow beneath them

issues.problem: The bright yellow prompt competes with the answer cards for first read during what is a vote-reveal beat.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 6 (one obvious focal point); minor -0.2
issues.fix: Dim the prompt to about 80% luminance while the reveal plays so the voted cards lead

issues.problem: Four stacked vote tags make the right card taller and heavier than the left, and the CLAIRE tag touches the card's corner tangent.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 7 (no awkward tangents); minor -0.2
issues.fix: Shift the tag stack 12 px inward and lower both cards 10 px to balance the headroom

issues.problem: Three display families (slab serif, hand-drawn caps, slab caps on tags) stand side by side with no clear scale step between the tag and author labels.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 8 (correct scale steps, disciplined type set); minor -0.2
issues.fix: Put the tags and author names on the same family at stepped sizes (16/22 px) so there are two families in total

issues.problem: The overlapping LUKE, LIZ and ANDY tags tuck under one another, which clips the edges of the tags and blurs where each one begins.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 9 (no clipping); minor -0.1
issues.fix: Space the tags on a 4 px gap with a consistent 2 px overlap instead of ad-hoc stacking

issues.problem: The swirl texture softens and loses its clay grain toward the frame edges compared with the crisply textured cards.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 10 (subtle grain, no blurry art); minor -0.2
issues.fix: Keep the fingerprint/grain detail normal map across the whole tunnel and limit depth blur to 1–2 px

issues.problem: The green PHIL, ALEX and LUKE tags are told apart mainly by hue next to the orange and red tags, which is weak under deuteranopia, though names and face glyphs help.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 11 (colour + glyph identity, CVD-safe); minor -0.2
issues.fix: Give each player a distinct pattern or icon on the tag and separate the green tags from red/orange by luminance (ΔL ≥ 20)

issues.problem: The vote result is implied only by the number of tags; no tally or winner mark states it outright.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 13 (result stated clearly); minor -0.2
issues.fix: Add a clay count badge (e.g. '4') on each card and a winner pop on the leading card

issues.problem: The flat, broadcast-style prompt text is the one element that lowers the premium handcrafted feel.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 15; minor -0.1
issues.fix: Integrate the prompt into a crafted plaque as in CAL-R1-01

issues.problem: The room code THBG is legible but small (about 30 px tall) and tucked into the corner, where a webcam overlay could clip it.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 17 (room code legible); minor -0.2
issues.fix: Move the code badge 24 px further inside the safe area and scale it up 20%

issues.problem: Faint haloing and softness show along the tag outlines and the card silhouettes.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 18 (no artefacts); minor -0.1
issues.fix: Render UI sprites at 2x with premultiplied alpha to remove the edge halos

issues.problem: The near-black wardrobe carcass is heavier and less textured than the warm wood and cardboard everywhere else, so it reads a little off from the rest of the handcrafted set.
issues.rule: RUBRIC item 1: one cohesive handcrafted world; §4.1 reference band minor flaw (0.1)
issues.fix: Lift the wardrobe body from near-black to a warm dark charcoal-brown (about #3a3440) and add the same 1-px highlight edge the desk uses.

issues.region: centre-left, desk items and small bed props
issues.problem: Small props (the pencil cup, the ruler, the blue gadget on the bed) blur into single-pixel clusters at 720p JPEG, so a second look is needed to read them.
issues.rule: RUBRIC item 2: subject reads within 1 s at 720p; §4.1 minor flaw (0.2)
issues.fix: Give the key small props a 1-px darker outline and at least 12 px at 720p, or cut the micro clutter that doesn't matter.

issues.problem: The saturated royal-blue chair seat is the one hot accent that pulls out of the otherwise muted warm and lavender palette.
issues.rule: RUBRIC item 3: controlled saturation; §4.1 'one hot accent' (0.2)
issues.fix: Desaturate the chair blue by about 20% toward the lavender backdrop hue (about #3f4fb0 → #4a52a0).

issues.problem: The light is mostly flat ambient. The contact shadows under the boxes and bed are weak, so the objects only lightly lift off the floor, although the soft ambient model is deliberate.
issues.rule: RUBRIC item 4: pieces lift off the surface; §4.1 minor flaw (0.2)
issues.fix: Add a 2–3 px tinted (purple-brown, not grey) contact shadow at the base of the boxes, the bed and the chair casters.

issues.problem: The thin black shelf brackets and rails are spindly next to the chunky boxes and furniture.
issues.rule: RUBRIC item 5: chunky toy silhouettes; §4.1 minor flaw (0.2)
issues.fix: Thicken the bracket strokes from 2 px to 3–4 px and round their corner joints.

issues.problem: The pink pig and the two tall box stacks compete for focus, so there is no single clear focal point.
issues.rule: RUBRIC item 6: one obvious focal point; §4.1 minor flaw (0.2)
issues.fix: Lower the contrast of the right box stack slightly, or add a soft light pool on the bed and pig so they read as the hero.

issues.problem: The red plaid shirt is high-contrast and draws a second look away from the centre of the room.
issues.rule: RUBRIC item 6: eye moves action → state → context; §4.1 minor flaw (0.2)
issues.fix: Darken the shirt red by about 10% and reduce its check contrast so it sits back as context.

issues.problem: The wardrobe top and the window blind roller make tangents with the top edge of the frame, so the crop feels a little tight at the top.
issues.rule: RUBRIC item 7: breathing room, no awkward tangents; §4.1 'a tangent' (0.2)
issues.fix: Pull the camera back or shift the frame down about 24 px so there is clear space above the wardrobe and window.

issues.problem: The floorboards are fairly flat, with sparse grain compared with the richer cardboard and brick textures.
issues.rule: RUBRIC item 10: materials read with subtle grain; §4.1 'one soft texture' (0.2)
issues.fix: Add 1-px darker grain streaks and a few knot details, varying by board, at about 8% contrast.

issues.problem: The flat blue checker backdrop feels slightly generic next to the richly detailed room.
issues.rule: RUBRIC item 15: premium indie gut check; §4.1 minor flaw (0.1)
issues.fix: Add a soft radial vignette and a subtle hue shift to the backdrop so it frames the room more warmly.

issues.problem: The diagonal glare streaks on the window have slightly stepped, aliased edges.
issues.rule: RUBRIC item 18: no aliasing; §4.1 minor flaw (0.1)
issues.fix: Redraw the glare lines with clean 1-px pixel-art diagonals (a 2:1 step pattern) and render at an integer scale.

issues.problem: The flat navy checkerboard backdrop outside the room cutaway looks like a generic UI tile. It is flatter and less handcrafted than the richly detailed pixel room, so it slightly weakens the one-world cohesion.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 1 (one cohesive art direction); §4.1 reference band minor flaw -0.1
issues.fix: Give the backdrop tiles the room's dithered shading and a subtle vignette, or swap it for a soft gradient in the wall's purple-blue hue.

issues.problem: The small props (the mouse pad, the pen cup, the blue item and cable on the bed) are only a few pixels wide. At 720p stream compression they blur together, so the second-read details are lost, though the room itself still reads instantly.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 2 (subject reads within 1 s at 720p); §4.1 minor flaw -0.2
issues.fix: Upscale key small props by about 1.25x, or add a 1 px darker outline around them so they hold up under JPEG q60.

issues.problem: The chair is a highly saturated primary blue, the hottest accent in the frame. It pulls away from the otherwise muted warm-wood and lavender palette. The wardrobe and desktop blacks also sit close to pure black.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 3 (controlled saturation, no pure black); §4.1 one hot accent -0.2
issues.fix: Lower the chair blue's saturation by about 15% and shift it toward the backdrop's indigo. Lift the darkest wardrobe tone to a tinted navy of about #2a2c3a.

issues.region: floor under boxes and chair, lower-centre ~y520-650
issues.problem: The ambient light is soft and deliberate, but the contact shadows under the box stack, chair and bed are faint. Objects lift only weakly off the floor, and the window gives no clear directional key.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 4 (pieces lift off via shadow); §4.1 minor flaw -0.2
issues.fix: Add a 2-3 px tinted (warm-brown, not grey) contact shadow under the boxes, chair base and bed frame. Add a faint light patch on the floor from the window.

issues.problem: The tall wardrobe is a hard, dark rectangular slab with crisp corners. It is the least toy-like silhouette in an otherwise chunky, soft form language.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 5 (chunky rounded silhouettes); §4.1 minor flaw -0.1
issues.fix: Add a 1 px highlight bevel on the wardrobe's top and front edges and round its top corners by 1-2 px.

issues.region: right 40% box stack vs centre bed
issues.problem: The large moving-box stack and the bed with the pig plush compete as the focal point with equal weight, so the eye hesitates before settling.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 6 (one obvious focal point); §4.1 minor flaw -0.2
issues.fix: Push the box stack slightly darker or cooler (about -8% value) so the plush and the open box on the bed become the single warm focal point.

issues.region: top-left corner, wardrobe top at y~45-100
issues.problem: The wardrobe's top edge and the room's cutaway wall run close to the upper frame edge. This creates a near-tangent with little breathing room, while the bottom-right has more free space.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 7 (breathing room, no awkward tangents); §4.1 tangent -0.2
issues.fix: Pan the camera down and right by about 24 px, or zoom out about 4%, so the wardrobe top clears the frame by 40 px or more.

issues.region: back walls, upper-centre and right ~x750-1200 y0-300
issues.problem: The pale lavender wall planes are almost flat fills with little grain or dither. Next to the textured wood, brick and cardboard, they read slightly as blank surfaces.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 10 (materials read, subtle grain); §4.1 one soft texture -0.1
issues.fix: Add a sparse 2-tone dither or faint plaster speckle (±3% value) to the wall planes.

issues.problem: This reads as premium indie. The only gap from 'nothing left to point to' is the generic backdrop around the cutaway, which feels like a template frame.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 15 (stranger believes premium indie); §4.1 minor flaw -0.1
issues.fix: Same fix as CAL-R1-01: give the backdrop a handcrafted treatment that matches the room.

issues.region: window glare streaks and chair outline, ~x530-700 y20-160 and y400-620
issues.problem: The pixel edges look slightly soft or uneven in places, which suggests non-integer scaling to 1280x720. The window streak diagonals also show uneven stair-stepping.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 18 (no aliasing or scaling artefacts); §4.1 minor flaw -0.2
issues.fix: Render at an integer scale with nearest-neighbour filtering (for example a 640x360 base at 2x) and redraw the glare streaks on clean 1:1 or 2:1 pixel diagonals.

issues.region: centre and left 40% (wind trails, waterfall streaks)
issues.problem: The smooth anti-aliased white wind-trail arcs and the long yellow light streak at bottom-right are drawn at sub-pixel resolution, so they break the chunky pixel grid that everything else sits on.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 1 (one cohesive art direction); §4.1 reference band, minor flaw noticed on a second look (0.2)
issues.fix: Draw the trails on the same 1 art-pixel grid (point-sampled, 2–3 art-px stroke), or render them into the low-res buffer before upscaling.

issues.problem: The dark navy character is only about 60 px wide and sits on mid-value foliage, so it takes a moment to find at 720p.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 2 (subject reads within 1 s); §4.1 minor flaw (0.2)
issues.fix: Add a 1 art-px light outline or rim to the character, or darken and desaturate the foliage by about 10% within a 120 px radius.

issues.region: centre, yellow fruit blobs around the character
issues.problem: Scattered saturated yellow discs of similar size compete with the character silhouette, which adds visual noise around the subject.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 2; §4.1 minor flaw (0.1)
issues.fix: Cut the density of yellow discs near the flight path by about 40%, or drop their saturation by 15%.

issues.problem: The waterfall foam flattens to near pure white with no tint, the one hot value in an otherwise warm-tinted palette.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 3 (no pure white; controlled palette); §4.1 minor flaw (0.1)
issues.fix: Tint the foam highlight to a pale aqua-cream (about #EAF6F0) instead of #FFFFFF.

issues.problem: The character gets no blob shadow on the ground or bridge below, so its height above the scene is implied only by the wind trails, and the lift is weaker than it could be.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 4 (pieces lift off the board); §4.1 minor flaw, second look (0.2)
issues.fix: Add a soft, tinted dark-olive drop shadow at about 25% opacity, offset down-right beneath the character.

issues.problem: A few rock silhouettes on the right have long straight diagonal edges that read slightly harder than the rounded tree clumps.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 5 (chunky, soft silhouettes); §4.1 minor flaw (0.1)
issues.fix: Break the long rock diagonals with 2–3 art-px notches or rounded corner steps.

issues.problem: The bright white-cyan waterfall is the highest-contrast mass in the frame and pulls the eye away from the character focal point.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 6 (one obvious focal point); §4.1 minor flaw, second look (0.2)
issues.fix: Lower the waterfall's peak value by about 10% and push the brightest contrast to the character.

issues.region: bottom-centre, bridge meeting the frame edge
issues.problem: The bridge runs straight into the bottom edge, which makes a tangent, and the character sits a little high of centre with little lead room in the direction of flight.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 7 (no awkward tangents); §4.1 minor flaw, second look (0.2)
issues.fix: Shift the camera about 40 px so the bridge ends inside or crosses the frame edge at an angle.

issues.problem: Large areas of mid-green foliage are flat fills with repeated round dither blobs, which read a little stamp-like next to the textured rock and bark.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 10 (no visible tiling, subtle grain); §4.1 minor flaw, second look (0.2)
issues.fix: Vary the blob size and hue by ±1 palette step and add sparse 1 art-px leaf-grain clusters.

issues.problem: At premium level overall, but the mixed-resolution trail lines are a small tell that keeps it just short of nothing-to-point-to.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 15; §4.1 minor flaw (0.1)
issues.fix: Pixel-snap all effects lines to the art grid (see CAL-R1-01).

issues.problem: The thin white and yellow effect lines show slight stair-step aliasing at shallow angles, set against the crisp pixel art.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 18 (no aliasing); §4.1 minor flaw (0.1)
issues.fix: Render the lines in the low-res pixel buffer, or use point-sampled 2 art-px strokes.

issues.problem: Soft round bokeh discs (yellow orbs, dark olive circles on the meadow) are a smooth, non-pixel overlay that sits slightly apart from the crisp hand-placed pixel art around them.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 1 (one cohesive art direction); §4.1 reference band, minor flaw −0.1
issues.fix: Quantise the orb/disc layer to the same pixel grid and palette (dithered 2–3 step edges) so it reads as part of the pixel world.

issues.problem: The character is small (~70 px wide) and its dark navy silhouette sits on mid-dark foliage, so the subject takes a second look to find at 720p.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 2 (subject reads instantly at 720p); §4.1 minor flaw −0.2
issues.fix: Add a 1-px light rim outline or a lighter ground patch behind the character to raise local contrast by ~30% luminance.

issues.problem: Yellow collectible orbs share value and saturation with the sunlit foliage highlights, adding noise near the subject.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 2; §4.1 minor flaw −0.1
issues.fix: Drop orb saturation ~15% or give them a 1-px warm-dark outline to separate from leaf highlights.

issues.problem: Waterfall foam goes to near-pure white in a large block, the one untinted hot spot in an otherwise warm-tinted palette.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 3 (no pure white, tinted values); §4.1 minor flaw −0.2
issues.fix: Tint the foam top value toward the palette's cream/aqua (~#EAF6F0) and keep pure white only for 1-px sparkles.

issues.problem: The character has no clear cast/blob shadow on the bridge planks, so it lifts off the ground less than the strong sun rays imply.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 4 (pieces lift off the surface); §4.1 minor flaw −0.2
issues.fix: Add a 2–3 px darker warm-brown ellipse shadow offset down-right under the character, matching the light-ray direction.

issues.problem: The grey cliff rocks top-right use large flat faceted polygons with hard straight edges that feel sharper than the rounded tree and bush shapes.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 5 (soft, chunky silhouettes); §4.1 minor flaw −0.2
issues.fix: Round rock silhouettes with 2–4 px stepped corners and add a soft highlight band on the upper-left edges.

issues.problem: The yellow orb trail and bright highlights around the character compete with it for first read; the swoosh lines help but the eye lands on the orbs first.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 6 (one obvious focal point); §4.1 minor flaw −0.2
issues.fix: Slightly darken/desaturate foliage within ~150 px of the character (vignette ~10%) so the character becomes the brightest-contrast element.

issues.problem: The long thin yellow light line running to the bottom-right corner pulls the eye out of frame away from the subject.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 6 (eye flow action → context); §4.1 minor flaw −0.1
issues.fix: Fade the ray's opacity to 0 over its last 40% before it reaches the frame edge.

issues.problem: The bridge runs straight off the bottom edge centre, a tangent that makes the lower frame feel cut rather than composed.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 7 (awkward tangents); §4.1 minor flaw −0.2
issues.fix: Shift camera ~40 px up or angle the bridge so it exits the frame off-centre (lower-third line).

issues.problem: The meadow's large soft circles read as flat blobs rather than grass texture, the one surface lacking material detail.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 10 (materials read, subtle grain); §4.1 minor flaw −0.2
issues.fix: Replace blob discs with clustered 2–3 px grass tufts and dithered shade patches in the meadow palette.

issues.problem: The soft bokeh/blob overlay is the one element that hints at a mixed technique on an otherwise premium frame.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 15 (premium indie gut check); §4.1 minor flaw −0.1
issues.fix: Same as CAL-R1-01: quantise the overlay to the pixel grid and palette.

issues.problem: The thin white motion arcs have slightly soft, sub-pixel edges that don't match the crisp integer-pixel art beneath.
issues.rule: RUBRIC §4.2 item 18 (no aliasing/filtering artefacts); §4.1 minor flaw −0.2
issues.fix: Render the arcs at native pixel resolution with nearest-neighbour upscaling (integer scale, no bilinear filtering).
